target: new: compound of two values (pubescent PATO_0000455 + hirsute FLOPO:0991050), with 'densely' as dense PATO_0001164 or a degree qualifier
reason: Two hairiness values joined, plus a density word. Each value already has a term, so no new class is needed.

target: new: compound of two values (elliptic PATO_0000947, EXACT synonym ellipsoid + flattened PATO_0002254)
reason: A flattened ellipsoid seed means both qualities hold, a conjunction of two existing terms rather than an intermediate between them.
'égalant le réceptacle' compares the androphore with the receptacle: equality to another part (ratio 1). 'égalant ou dépassant' is an alternative of two such relations (pattern 07).
'sans gibbosités' says the banner petal is not swollen on one side. A gibbosity is a shape, not a PO part, so this is a negated value, not the absence of a part.
'Many-headed' is an indefinite count of heads (capitulum inflorescence PO_0030121, 'numerous') in the inflorescence or glomerule, like 'few-flowered'.
French rhomboïdal = rhomboid, diamond-shaped. 'cylindrique à rhomboïdal' is a continuum handled separately.

target: new: compound of two values (obtuse PATO_0001935, EXACT synonym roundish + oblique, i.e. asymmetric)
reason: A rounded and unequal-sided leaflet or pod apex: two qualities of different kinds. PATO oblique orientation (PATO_0002481) is an orientation, not this asymmetry.
Mistranslation: the source 'subéperonnées à la base' means slightly spurred, not slightly prickly. One example also has the broken bearer 'part:'. A rule would mislabel genuine 'subechinate'.

target: new: compound of two values (apical dehiscence + extrorse FLOPO:0991165, approximate per docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md)
reason: Anthers that open at the apex and somewhat outwards: an orientation value already in FLOPO, with 'sub-' and a position. Not a single quality.
Same reading as 'indistinct' in the previous review (C175): not clearly visible. 'à peine distinct' is the French form.
The stipule or bract ends in two acuminate points: a count of 2 apical points, each acuminate (PATO_0002228), like 'bilobed'. Too rare and composite for a term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum) or new: compound of two values (scalloped PATO_0001889, EXACT synonym crenate + lobed PATO_0001979)
reason: A margin with small rounded lobes: two margin values of one attribute. '5-7-crenate-lobulate' adds a count (pattern 03).

target: new: compound of two values (hirsute FLOPO:0991050 + scabrous FLOPO:0991058)
reason: Hairy and rough to the touch: two existing values of different attributes.
Like an ocrea, a tubular sheath round the stem. This is what sheathing defines: a base wrapping the axis with its margins meeting or fused. PO has no ocrea class.
'en forme de sac' and 'sac-shaped' = saccate, shaped like a pouch or bag.

target: new: compound of two values (sericeous PATO_0104358 + ferruginous colour of the hairs)
reason: Silky hairs that are rust-coloured: a hairiness value and a colour, which is a conjunction. PATO rusty (PATO_0070059) is oxidation, not a colour. The keel example is a long fragment.

target: new: compound of two values (tomentose PATO_0002341 + ferruginous colour of the indumentum)
reason: 'tomenteuses-ferrugineuses' = tomentum that is rust-coloured. A conjunction of hairiness and colour. Not PATO_0070059 rusty, which is a texture from oxidation.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum) or new: compound of two values (truncated PATO_0000936 + auriculate PATO_0001981)
reason: A base that is truncate with small auricles at the corners: two existing base-shape values combined.
Rare and unclear: 'atténué en biseau' (a margin tapering obliquely) and a keeled grass-like leaf edge are different things. No clear quality for a rule or term.

target: new: compound of two values (puberulous FLOPO:0991049 + hairs appressed FLOPO:0991064), with 'densely' as dense PATO_0001164 or a degree qualifier
reason: Finely hairy with hairs lying flat, densely: existing values, where 'appressed' applies to the hairs. No new term needed.
Bark 'poussiéreux' or 'semblant saupoudrée d'une poussière' is a powdery, mealy surface, as farinose (C223). 'seed: dusty' probably means minute dust-like seeds and should not take this rule.
'faussement / falsamente terminales' is exactly pseudoterminal: appearing terminal but arising laterally. 'false terminal' is already a synonym there.

'stamen: filaments equal' = the filaments (PO_0009067) are of equal size, so the bearer moves to filament. 'corona: filaments égalant ± le tube' is a comparison with another part (pattern 10) and does not take this rule.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (part of the part: vascular bundle PO_0005020 + slender PATO_0002212)
reason: 'à fine nervation' says the veins of the blade, bract or corolla are fine: a quality of a part of the bearer, not a new quality. Fallback is the 'veined' rule (vascular bundle present).
French and Spanish plural of involute (rolled inwards): PATO_0001962.

target: new: compound of two values (lanceolate shape + apiculate apex)
reason: An outline shape and a tip shape of the anther joined: a conjunction. 'apiculate' itself has no value class; the PATO lexicon has it only as a synonym of the attribute sharpness PATO_0000944.

label: longistylous
definition: A heterostylous quality inhering in a flower by virtue of its being of the long-styled morph, with the stigmas held above the anthers.
reason: A real botanical quality, the pin morph of heterostylous species. No term exists; distylous (FLOPO:0991260) is the species-level quality. Sibling brevistylous would follow.
Veins running lengthwise, parallel along the sepal, bract or tunic, the same reading as 'parallel-veined' (C341). 'en relief' or 'bien visible' are separate qualities.

target: new: degree modifier on a value (apiculate with a long point)
reason: 'longuement apiculées' = apiculate with a long apiculus, a degree on a value. 'apiculate' has no value class, only a synonym of the attribute sharpness PATO_0000944, which should be fixed first.
'longuement engainantes' = leaves with a long sheath. The quality is sheathing; 'longly' is a degree that can stay in the record as a qualifier.
